claims.text: Machine learning can predict optimal RHEA compositions combining strength, ductility, and low weight.
Existing RHEAs have varying compositions and properties.
Machine-learning algorithms can be applied to existing RHEA composition and mechanical-property data.
The training data must cover a wide range of RHEA compositions.
The training data must include corresponding mechanical properties.
Machine-learning models can identify patterns and correlations between RHEA compositions and properties.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn from existing RHEA data to predict the performance of new compositions.
Predicted performance can guide the design of RHEAs with desired properties.
The machine-learning model will identify RHEA compositions with improved strength relative to traditionally designed compositions.
The machine-learning model will identify RHEA compositions with improved ductility relative to traditionally designed compositions.
The machine-learning model will identify RHEA compositions with reduced weight relative to traditionally designed compositions.
Current alloy-design methods use empirical testing and simulations.
The proposed approach is limited to refractory high-entropy alloys and their mechanical properties.
The effectiveness of machine learning for RHEA design depends on the quality and quantity of available data.
